internal.title: Investigation of Kafka Consumer Lag and Latency in Accounting Service
internal.body:
At 10:56 UTC, an alert for high Kafka consumer lag was triggered on the accounting service. Initial diagnosis rounds identified latency issues within the accounting service as the primary cause, supported by high consumer lag (5200 records) and elevated p95 latency (0.12 seconds) with a low error rate (0.2%). Secondary hypotheses considered Kafka latency and potential resource exhaustion in accounting, but these were less supported or inconclusive due to system constraints and proposal refusals by guardrails.

The incident was escalated for further investigation. No immediate resolution was applied during this timeframe, and the root cause remains under investigation. Monitoring continues to ensure system stability and to detect any recurrence of the issue.

Key timeline events:
- 10:56:26 UTC: Alert received for KafkaConsumerLagHigh
- 11:16:08 UTC: Diagnosis round 1 focused on accounting latency
- 11:16:22 UTC: Diagnosis round 2 focused on Kafka latency
- 11:16:34 UTC: Diagnosis round 3 revisited accounting latency

Actions taken included hypothesis testing and proposal submissions, some of which were refused due to guardrail constraints.

Further updates will be provided as the investigation progresses.

external.title: Intermittent Latency Affecting Accounting Service Processing
external.body:
Between 10:56 and 11:20 UTC, the accounting service experienced intermittent latency issues causing delays in processing Kafka messages. This resulted in a backlog of messages being processed more slowly than usual. Our teams identified the latency as the primary factor and are actively investigating the underlying cause.

We are monitoring the situation closely to prevent any impact on service availability or data integrity. We apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused and appreciate your patience as we work to resolve the issue.
